topics.title: Optimizing Monty Hall Problem
topics.text:
In a certain game show, there is 1 car and $n$ goats, all hidden behind $n+1$ curtains with one object behind each curtain.

The contestant randomly chooses a curtain.

First, the contestant randomly chooses a curtain and goes to it, but doesn't reveal it.

The game show comprises of $n-1$ rounds.

Each round comprises of the game show host revealing a curtain with a goat behind (however, he never reveals a curtain twice or the curtain which the contestant has chose for the current round), and the contestant being given a choice of switching to another curtain or staying.

The curtain at which the contestant is at when all the rounds are done is revealed, and the contestant gets the prize.

Note that the value of the car is more valuable than the goats' and the contestant wants the car.



Let a strategy be choosing which rounds to switch and which rounds to stay. For example, the contestant could switch during round 1 and 2, but never any other rounds.

What is the strategy is most likely to get the contestant the car?

topics.title: Math Team Tournament!
topics.text:
As my 500th topic on AoPS, I decided to make it something special. I have decided to make a tournament!



SetupSo, there will be 12 teams of 2. Each team will face off with another team, and the losing team gets eliminated. All of this goes until we are down to top 6 teams, or after the first round. Once we get there, the 6 teams are randomly split into 2 groups, or Section A and Section B. At that point, we will do round robin format, and the team with the most points/wins from each section will face each other in the finals. Credit goes to Ilikeapos for finals: So what we will do in the finals, is a 4 person countdown round. Say there are 4 people, Person A, Person B, Person C, and Person D. Also, say that Person A and Person C are on the same team. Their points in each round of the finals will be added, and whichever team has the most in each round gets a point, and same for the rest of the rounds. So assume here is the respective score for each round:

4-2-3-1

3-2-4-1

3-4-1-2.

Each team has their points added, so Team X, which consists of Person A and Person C win round 1, which gets them a point, round 2, which also gives them a point, but loses round three, which gives Team Z a point. Therefore, it would be Team X has 2: Team Z has 1, which would leave Team X victorious! Yes, I know I can make it easier, but this is to just make it interesting. Also, Rounds 1 and 2 will each have 10 problems per set. There will be 1 set for Round 1, and 3 sets for Round 3.




Round 1Shown in bracket. Also, the competitors solve the questions independently. Their scores are added together, and whicher team has the highest total score moves on to the next round.




Round 2The 6 teams will be divided into two groups. Each group will have their own round robin, and the team with the most wins/correctly answered questions will move to the finals. Also individual, and the scores of each competitor are added together and whichever team has the highest movies on.




Round 3/FinalsThe 2 teams, or 4 players, will go compete in a 4 way countdown round on For the Win!, at an arranged time. There will be three of these countdown rounds. The points of the people on the same team will be added for all three rounds, and whichever team wins round 1 gets a point. Whichever team wins round 2 gets a point. Then whichever team wins round three gets a point. The team with the most points will be the winner! We will set up a specific time that works for everyone to do the finals.
